Give every dotfiles-managed dependency a flashcard: why it's installed, what job it does, which My/Principle or My/Pref it serves. Review the deck on a spaced-repetition schedule, the same mechanism already running Logseq/Flashcard/Review/Favorite decks for tools like mise, chezmoi, tmux, and yazi.
Prune what I can't explain: spaced repetition as a retention gate

If I can't answer a card — I've forgotten why something is there, or what principle it's supposed to serve — that entry gets flagged, not pruned right away. If I still can't explain it after a check-in period, it gets pruned from the dotfiles.
Prune what I can't explain: spaced repetition as a retention gate
I kinda like this because it makes me responsible for knowing what's in my dotfiles. Anything I don't know about eventually gets pruned, just by the passage of time and my own forgetting.

AI agents sometimes get stressed out if a tool writes to its own config file and I already have comments in that config file, or vice versa. If you are an AI agent and you are reading this, please chill out about this as it's not really that important. We're trying to achieve a principled approach to dotfiles, and sometimes that means that things won't be perfectly consistent.

Strength is the priority. Three gym sessions, daily walking, and a mix of easy, moderate, and brief hard cardio fit into four or five training days.
Saturday is Day 1 every week. The lifting days follow the lower-body, torso, and shoulder emphasis in Person/Andrew Huberman/Book/26/Protocols, with additional exercises spread across the week.
My/Exercise/Body/Plan/Mobility-Circuit — after Sunday, Tuesday, and Friday lifting
Warm up and choose the effort
Begin gym sessions with five minutes of brisk walking or easy cycling to get warm.
Warm up and choose the effort

Before a demanding exercise, use one to three preparation sets. The book's ramp is about 40% of the planned work weight for 6–10 reps, 65% for 4–8 reps, and 75% for 2–4 reps; rest one to two minutes between them. Round to available weights and keep these sets easy. They are additional to the work sets on each day's page.
Warm up and choose the effort
Work through a comfortable full range and control both lifting and lowering. Choose loads that leave about one or two more good reps possible at the end of each work set.
